messages:
dylan: Heads up — noticed a cluster of 429s for acct `org-8675` around 15:02 UTC. Metering pipeline shows the tokens arrive ~30s after the enforcer rejected requests. Suspect stale burst/window state on the enforcer when metering is lagging.

jess-engineer: Can you paste a short timeline and any enforcer logs?

dylan: timeline: request at 15:02:01 -> enforcer reject (429) at 15:02:02 -> metering ingest shows events 15:02:33. Enforcer log: `rate_limit_check: key=org-8675, window_start=15:01:00, used=1000, limit=1000, decision=reject` even though the events that made used=1000 only landed later.

nina-sre: This matches the "ingest lag causes enforcement to see stale lower counts" pattern. We're seeing bursts where ingestion batching pushes counts behind enforcement.

kevin: Do we have a metric that correlates enforcer rejects with metering lag? I can query Prometheus.

jess-engineer: Quick Prom query that helped earlier: `sum by (env) (increase(metering_ingest_backlog_events_total[2m]))` and `enforcer_rejects_total{reason="quota"}`. If backlog > 0 and rejects spike, we likely have a race.

kevin: Ran a quick ad-hoc: backlog spiked ~20k events between 15:01:50-15:02:40 and enforcer_rejects increased by 120 in same window. Looks correlated.

maria-l: Two possible fixes: 1) Enforcer reads last-known counters from a fast read path (local cache + optimistic leases) and accepts short grace when metering backlog > threshold. 2) Make metering ingest near-realtime (harder infra work). Prefer (1) short-term.

jess-engineer: Agreed. Concrete proposal for (1): if `metering_ingest_lag_seconds > 5s` for X seconds, then enforcer allows ephemeral burst capacity equal to pending events for that key up to a safety cap (e.g., 200 tokens) and emits a shadow-accounting event for reconciliation. Pseudocode: ```if backlog_for_key(key) > 0 and ingest_lag > 5: allow_grace = min(pending_events_estimate(key), 200) decision=allow_shadow(reason="ingest-lag-grace")```

nina-sre: We should also emit a metric `enforcer_ingest_grace_allowed_total{reason="ingest-lag"}` and tag the key so the backfill job can reconcile later. Otherwise accounting will be inconsistent.

kevin: Concern: this relaxes enforcement under high lag; could allow abuse. Mitigations: cap the max grace, limit rate of grace per org per minute, and require shadow events for all allowed requests. Also add a short TTL (30s) on the ephemeral allowance.

maria-l: +1 on TTL and caps. Ops playbook: if backlog > X for > 2m, set temporary global throttle to protect backend and notify oncall. This keeps abuse window small.

jess-engineer: Plan: I'll open a small PR to enforcer runtime with the graceful allowance + metrics + shadow flag. Nina can run a canary in staging. If green, we roll to prod with a 1% rollout then 10% then global.

nina-sre: I'll take canary and create a Grafana panel: `enforcer_ingest_grace_allowed_total`, `metering_ingest_backlog_events_total`, `enforcer_rejects_total`. Will add alert: if rejects don't drop after grace enabled -> rollback.

dylan: thanks — in the short term, can we also add a dashboard card showing 'recent backlog per shard' in console so support can see this when customers file tickets?

maria-l: I'll make a tiny console widget — just a per-shard backlog sparkline. Low effort.

enforcer-bot: deploy check: vulnerable paths: enforcer/ratecheck.go, metrics/reporting.go. Suggested test cases: 1) burst with ingest delayed 30s -> requests allowed up to cap and shadowed. 2) normal flow unchanged.

jess-engineer: I'll target the PR today (link will follow). Owners: jess-engineer (implementation), nina-sre (canary + dashboards), maria-l (console widget), kevin (prom queries/alerts). Marking this for follow-up in eng-oncall rotation notes. :thumbsup:
